summary.intent: Get callisto's stalled self-release (0.8.0) fixed and verified after a prior agent's mess, then clean up the repo (docs, specs, plans, branches), decide the open owner items, and consolidate the published crates.
summary.outcome: Verified PR #104's checksum fix and found its receipt-rename premise false; confirmed a P0 where plan's swallowed jq failure leaves has_artifacts empty and silently skips the release, with a fix prototyped but not pushed. Opened docs cleanup PR #151 (merged), deleted 173 local branches, and made decisions on crate consolidation. Built PR #157 merging 8 published crates into 4 (callisto-model, manifests, graph, cli), rebased on top of #156 and #158 with 1639 tests passing; #113 (0.9.0) is still open.

repo: GitHub skips any job with a skipped transitive ancestor unless its own `if` contains a status function, so jobs with needs must use always() plus explicit needs.X.result == 'success'.

`echo "x=$(cmd)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT` under `set -euo pipefail` swallows cmd failure because echo's exit status wins; assign to a variable in its own statement and validate with a case. Only one such instance exists across .github.

upload-artifact name uniqueness is scoped per run attempt: run 34702634375 uploaded the same `release-intent` name successfully in attempts 1-3, so the per-attempt receipt rename in #104 rests on a false premise.

The policy script .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh has a scheduler simulator and --self-test mutants (30 on #104); its scenarios never feed an empty job output, so it cannot see the empty has_artifacts class.

Release gate relies on a merged managed PR from callisto/version-packages, a GitHub-verified signed commit, and protected main (ruleset 22292852); the decision-file digest is unkeyed, which was accepted as an ADR candidate.

`callisto-core` and `callisto` are taken on crates.io by an unrelated owner (Ganryuu); decision was to keep callisto-model and fold format and vcs into it, and fold conventional and changelog into graph.
The Release PR #113 is bot-opened with GITHUB_TOKEN, so it runs no checks; CI doesn't listen to merge_group and the main ruleset's required-checks list is empty.
Orin-dx/actions setup-rust runs floating Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 inside release jobs with publish tokens, which verify-action-pins.sh cannot see.
The 'Install Moon' step in setup-callisto also installs the consumer's .prototools toolchain; oxc-react-codegen's npm publish relies on it, so it was renamed rather than removed.
Clippy map_err_ignore only catches `|_|`; 14 `|_err|` style sites remain in src/ and an architecture test in graph flags dropped error sources.
Cargo.toml:6 has a stale `[workspace.package] version = "0.3.3"` that is unused because no crate uses version.workspace = true.
Build time was unchanged by the crate merge: clean build 16s before and 15s after, single-file edits about 3s.

code.finding: The has_artifacts echo with an embedded jq command substitution swallows jq failure and emits an empty output, which makes build-artifact, build and execute all skip while the run reports success.
execute adds --artifact-manifest only if manifest.json exists, with no else branch; the Rust side was checked and the hunter's 'silent artifact-less release' claim was refuted.
The rule requires github.run_attempt in the receipt artifact name and asserts a collision that does not occur on the platform.
The generator adds red/yellow/green emojis to the Bump column; the owner confirmed these basic severity markers are fine and the AGENTS.md rule targets superfluous emojis.

friction: The user said another AI agent made a mess, but repo state matched the handoff exactly, so the real problems had to be found by auditing the workflow and PR #104.
The hunter reports were truncated and needed follow-up messages, and one hunter produced a circular, false finding.
A concurrent Claude session was doing an overlapping docs cleanup (feat/docs-cleanup, then #153), creating overlap and conflict risk with #151.
The GitHub token lacked the delete_repo scope, so the rehearsal repo deletion fell to the user.
Rebasing #157 onto #156/#158 hit six code conflicts in files the fix PRs also edit (groups.rs, cascade.rs, apply.rs, aggregate.rs, version.rs, cli pre.rs).
The crates.io name callisto-core was unavailable, forcing a change of plan.
open_items: Apply the P0 fix to the has_artifacts step on #104 or a new PR, with a policy rule and mutant that feed an empty output; not yet pushed and awaiting the user's go-ahead.
#104 still needs a code-owner review or owner bypass; the 0.8.0 release itself has not been verified end to end (no tags, crates, or GitHub Release).
Decide whether to keep or revert the per-attempt receipt rename and correct the false rationale in the comment and policy error string.
Merge order for the stack is #156, #158, then #157; #113 (0.9.0) should wait so it releases as four crates.
Roadmap item 7 follow-up: publish a final release of each retired crate (format, vcs, conventional, changelog) whose README points to its new home.
Review #153 (one current-behavior spec per area, ADRs, v1 fix plan), which supersedes the roadmap from #151.

Open decisions: build or drop the error-source gate (recommended build), drop the mode-derived tag template (recommended), accept release-commit provenance as an ADR, pin Swatinem/rust-cache in orin-dx/actions, and make the bot PR tested via merge_group.
Optionally update AGENTS.md's emoji rule to say 'no superfluous emojis'; delete the empty `release` environment; remove stale canon/vector/lambda plugins from .claude/settings.json.
Token rotation was deferred by the user; trusted publishing via OIDC remains an option.
Fix the stale `[workspace.package] version = "0.3.3"` in Cargo.toml, and remove the stray LICENSE-APACHE files (planned in PR 7).
Unpublished 0.6.0-0.7.2 backfill and the release notes for breaking changes between 0.5.0 and 0.8.0 remain the owner's call.
